title: MACSEC: Show MACsec encapsulation
description: Show MACsec encapsulation in the protocol column for commonly used protocols.

notes.body: I am not a fan of this. The whole purpose of the packet list is to show the top level protocol information. This will open up a can-o-worms where every underlying protocol, transport or otherwise, will feel the need to be represented here. Also the indiscriminate nature of which protocol get to be listed in combination is ambiguous at best. What list makes sense to one, does not make sense to others, given the wide scope of application of Wireshark. Therefore my -1.
That's fine with me.  This is something I had put together as part of the original submission.  Feel free to ignore/decline/delete.
That's really smart and I didn't know you could do that.  But we're going to drop this anyhow.
I am not sure that this is necessary, but if you want to do it the simpler way is to do what GTP does and prepend the string to the protocol column upon success.
I think this was covered in another commit. If not please open a new mr with relevant parts.

changes_data.diff:
@@ -134,7 +134,7 @@ typedef struct _packet_info {
                                        unknown (P2P_DIR_UNKNOWN) */
 
   GHashTable *private_table;    /**< a hash table passed from one dissector to another */
-
+  const char *encapsulated;     /**< when not NULL, updates the protocol column to indicate the packet was encapsulated by prepending this string */
   wmem_list_t *layers;          /**< layers of each protocol */
   wmem_map_t *proto_layers;     /** map of proto_id to curr_proto_layer_num. */
   uint8_t curr_layer_num;        /**< The current "depth" or layer number in the current frame */
